title: The order of execution of the formAssociatedCallback hook does not match the implementations
body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard? The specification says [the following](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#custom-element-reactions): > When the user agent [resets the form owner](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#reset-the-form-owner) of a [form-associated custom element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#form-associated-custom-element) and doing so changes the form owner, its formAssociatedCallback is called, given the new form owner (or null if no owner) as an argument. That is, the call to the `formAssociatedCallback` hook occurs when 2 actions are performed: - Calling the [reset the form owner](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#reset-the-form-owner) algorithm - Changing the form owner Now let's list the cases that call the [reset the form owner](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#reset-the-form-owner): 1) [Insertion steps](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-trees:concept-node-insert-ext) 2) [Removing steps](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-trees:concept-node-remove-ext) 3) [Moving steps](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-trees:concept-node-move-ext) 4) [Any modification of the form attribute of the listed form-associated element, as well as any modifications related to the ID that may entail a change in the owner of the form](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#association-of-controls-and-forms) 5) [Upgrade element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-upgrade-an-element) I am only interested in the first 3 points (in 4 and 5 I did not find any inconsistencies with the implementations). --- Let's see under what conditions [reset the form owner](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#reset-the-form-owner) is called. [**Insertion steps**](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-trees:concept-node-insert-ext) > 2) If insertedNode is a [form-associated element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#form-associated-element) or the ancestor of a [form-associated element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#form-associated-element), then: > > 1) If the [form-associated element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#form-associated-element)'s [parser inserted flag](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#parser-inserted-flag) is set, then return. > > 2) [Reset the form owner](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#reset-the-form-owner) of the [form-associated element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#form-associated-element). The [reset the form owner](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#reset-the-form-owner) call always occurs for the [form-associated element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#form-associated-element). [**Removing steps**](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-trees:concept-node-remove-ext) и [**Moving steps**](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-trees:concept-node-move-ext) > If movedNode is a [form-associated element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#form-associated-element) or the ancestor of a [form-associated element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#form-associated-element), then: > > 1. If the [form-associated element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#form-associated-element) has a [form owner](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#form-owner) and the [form-associated element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#form-associated-element) and its [form owner](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#form-owner) are no longer in the same [tree](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree), then [reset the form owner](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#reset-the-form-owner) of the [form-associated element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#form-associated-element). The [reset the form owner](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#reset-the-form-owner) call occurs if the [form owner](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#form-owner) is not null and the [form-associated element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#form-associated-element) and its [form owner](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#form-owner) are in different trees There are no problems for [removing steps](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-trees:concept-node-remove-ext), because before its execution in the [remove](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-remove) algorithm, the node is removed from the tree in which it was. Now the tree of the removed node is itself. And here is the problem that concerns the specification. > [!WARNING] > For the [moving steps](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-trees:concept-node-move-ext) the problem is divided into two parts: > - Moving a [form-associated element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#form-associated-element) from one tree to another. > > For example: If a [form-associated element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#form-associated-element) has a [form owner](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#form-owner) value of null, and the element is placed in a form, then the condition for the [reset the form owner](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#reset-the-form-owner) will not be met because the [form owner](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#form-owner) for the [form-associated element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#form-associated-element) is null. > - Moving a [form-associated elements](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#form-associated-element) within the same tree. > > For example: If a [form-associated element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#form-associated-element) has a [form owner](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#form-owner) value of null, and the element is placed in a form. The condition for the [reset the form owner](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#reset-the-form-owner) will not be met for two reasons. The first is that the [form owner](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#form-owner) is null, and the second is because we are in the same tree. It seems to me that the condition for the [reset the form owner](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#reset-the-form-owner) algorithm in the [moving steps](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-trees:concept-node-move-ext) should simply be removed. Opinion? --- It is also worth clarifying that in all three algorithms the order of `formAssociatedCallback` comes before any of `connectedCallback`, `disconnectedCallback` and `connectedMoveCallback`. Here are excerpts from the specification. For [move](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#move): > 24. For each [shadow-including inclusive descendant](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-shadow-including-inclusive-descendant) inclusiveDescendant of node, in [shadow-including tree order](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-shadow-including-tree-order): > > 1. If inclusiveDescendant is node, then run the [moving steps](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-move-ext) with inclusiveDescendant and oldParent. Otherwise, run the [moving steps](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-move-ext) with inclusiveDescendant and null. > > > Because the [move](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#move) algorithm is a separate primitive from [insert](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-insert) and [remove](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-remove), it does not invoke the traditional [insertion steps](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-insert-ext) or [removing steps](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-remove-ext) for inclusiveDescendant. > > 2. If inclusiveDescendant is [custom](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-custom) and newParent is [connected](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#connected), then [enqueue a custom element callback reaction](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/custom-elements.html#enqueue-a-custom-element-callback-reaction) with inclusiveDescendant, callback name "connectedMoveCallback", and « ». For [insert](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-insert): > 7. For each [shadow-including inclusive descendant](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-shadow-including-inclusive-descendant) inclusiveDescendant of node, in [shadow-including tree order](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-shadow-including-tree-order): > > 1. Run the [insertion steps](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-insert-ext) with inclusiveDescendant. > > 2. If inclusiveDescendant is [connected](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#connected): > > 1. If inclusiveDescendant is [custom](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-custom), then [enqueue a custom element callback reaction](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/custom-elements.html#enqueue-a-custom-element-callback-reaction) with inclusiveDescendant, callback name "connectedCallback", and « ». > > 2. Otherwise, [try to upgrade](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/custom-elements.html#concept-try-upgrade) inclusiveDescendant. > > > If this successfully upgrades inclusiveDescendant, its connectedCallback will be enqueued automatically during the [upgrade an element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/custom-elements.html#concept-upgrade-an-element) algorithm. For [remove](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-remove): > 11. Run the [removing steps](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-remove-ext) with node and parent. > > 12. Let isParentConnected be parent’s [connected](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#connected). > > 13. If node is [custom](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-custom) and isParentConnected is true, then [enqueue a custom element callback reaction](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/custom-elements.html#enqueue-a-custom-element-callback-reaction) with node, callback name "disconnectedCallback", and « ». > > > It is intentional for now that [custom](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-custom) [elements](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element) do not get parent passed. This might change in the future if there is a need. > > 14. For each [shadow-including descendant](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-shadow-including-descendant) descendant of node, in [shadow-including tree order](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-shadow-including-tree-order): > > 1. Run the [removing steps](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-remove-ext) with descendant and null. > > 2. If descendant is [custom](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-custom) and isParentConnected is true, then [enqueue a custom element callback reaction](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/custom-elements.html#enqueue-a-custom-element-callback-reaction) with descendant, callback name "disconnectedCallback", and « ». --- Now to the main thing. I checked [insertBefore](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-node-insertbefore) and [moveBefore](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-parentnode-movebefore) in Chrome (for Firefox I could only check [insertBefore](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-node-insertbefore), since [moveBefore](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-parentnode-movebefore) is not yet available there). I was surprised by the results. The order of `formAssociatedCallback`, `connectedCallback` and `disconnectedCallback` differs between browsers, and Chrome does not follow the order specified in the specification at all. Here is an example: ```html
element
``` If you click on `btn2` in Chrome you will see this: ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/52e0d631-15b1-4459-b0f2-d2841dddd1ca) For Firefox the situation is different: ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/84c8f7de-6a41-478d-b57f-2da6ed19499e) In both browsers it should be in this order: - `formAssociatedCallback` - `disconnectedCallback` - `formAssociatedCallback` - `connectedCallback` Also if you click on `btn4` in Chrome you will see this: ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e73d2422-ee14-4565-b317-84cf9e6fd9bb) But only `connectedMoveCallback` should be called. What went wrong? I have attached a demoscene at this [link](https://strong-supreme-rail.glitch.me/) (open the console and see 8 cases of different DOM manipulations). --- To summarize everything written, there are 2 problems: - The implementations either do not correspond to the order of calling the `formAssociatedCallback` hook or correspond, but partially. - The problem of determining the [moving steps](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-trees:concept-node-move-ext) for the [form-associated custom element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#form-associated-custom-element), the [reset the form owner](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#reset-the-form-owner) algorithm will not be called if the element was moved outside the form from form or, conversely, moved in the form within the same tree. @domfarolino
